server.instructions: TK is a personal knowledge base. Use these tools to search and retrieve documents from the user's collection, as well as documents shared with them via libraries and direct shares. You can also create new documents.

tools.description: Add an existing document to a library. The user must own the document and be a member of the library. IMPORTANT: Adding a document to a library makes it visible to ALL members of that library. This may change a document from private (visible only to the owner) to shared. Confirm with the user before calling this, especially for libraries with multiple members.

document_id.description: The UUID of the document to add.

library_id.description: The UUID of the library to add the document to.

tools.name: add_document_to_library

tools.description:
Create the user's Daily Note for a date, with content. The note is built the way the app builds it — from the user's daily-note template when they use one — and 'content' is added after the template's sections. Use this instead of create_document when the user wants something recorded in their daily note, today's note, or a specific day's note. 

This FAILS if the day already has a Daily Note; the error carries that note's id and the existing content is left untouched. When that happens, call get_daily_note with format "json" for node ids and then edit_document — do not retry this tool. 

'content' is required: an empty Daily Note is identical to the one the app creates when the user opens that day, so there is nothing worth creating. The title comes from the template (usually the formatted date); there is no title parameter. With a template, the first call of the day may take a while.

content.description: Markdown added after the template's sections, WITHOUT a title heading (the note's heading comes from the template). Required — unlike create_document, there is no useful empty daily note.

date.description: The note's date as YYYY-MM-DD, in the user's LOCAL timezone. Required — the server has no timezone, so it cannot resolve 'today' itself, and a note written to the wrong day cannot be undone; if you do not know the user's local date, ask.

skip_writing_prompt.description: Set true to create the note without a daily writing prompt, e.g. when the note is a generated briefing. Permanent for that note. Omit to follow the user's writing-prompt setting.

tags.description: Tags to organize and categorize the note.

tools.name: create_daily_note

tools.description: Create a new document in the user's personal knowledge base. The document body MUST be passed in the 'content' parameter as markdown (converted automatically); calls with unrecognized parameters (e.g. 'file_text', 'body') are rejected. If no content is provided, a minimal document with the title as a heading is created. The response includes content_length and heading/paragraph counts — verify these match what you sent (content_length 0 means the document body is empty; heading_count includes the title heading, so a content with one heading reports heading_count 2).

collapsed_sections.description: Exact heading text of sections that should start collapsed for you when the document is created (e.g. an appendix or raw-data section, while the summary stays open). Match the heading text exactly as written in content. Omit to leave all sections expanded.

content.description: The content of the document in markdown format. If omitted, a minimal document with the title as a heading is created.

library_id.description: UUID of a library to add the document to after creation. Pass this when the user says 'in [library]', 'add to [library]', or 'put in [library]'. Do NOT pass this when the user says 'for [library]' — that is ambiguous and likely means a personal draft. NOTE: Adding the document to a library makes it visible to ALL library members, changing it from private to shared. Confirm with the user first.

tags.description: Tags to organize and categorize the document.

title.description: The title of the document. Must be non-empty.

tools.name: create_document

tools.description:
Make surgical, merge-safe edits to part of a document without replacing its whole body. Unlike update_document (a whole-body replace that drops any content not in the new body, including a collaborator's unsaved edits), each op here is resolved against the LIVE document and only touches the node you target, so it merges safely with concurrent edits and preserves everything else (including per-user heading collapse state). Prefer this over update_document whenever you are changing a specific part of a document rather than rewriting the whole thing. Requires editor access: the owner, or a user the document is shared with as an editor. SHARED DOCUMENTS: if anyone else can already see the document — its owner or other share recipients, a public link, profile sharing, or a library with other members — the first call changes nothing and returns an error saying how it is shared. Tell the user, and ask whether to go ahead; only after they agree, call again with confirm_shared: true. Never set confirm_shared without asking the user first. 

Addressing: ops target nodes by their UUID. Get node UUIDs by first calling get_document_content with format:"json" — the Tiptap content nodes carry an attrs.id you pass as node_id / anchor_node_id. search_document_content also returns node_id for matching passages. 

Op types:
- replace_node_text: replace the substring matched by original_text inside node_id with new_text (plain text only). original_text must match the node's current text (whitespace is normalized); if it isn't found the op is rejected so you can re-read and retry.
- replace_node_contents: replace the ENTIRE inline content of node_id with content (markdown supporting inline formatting like **bold**, _italic_, and links). It keeps the node and its id, so this is the op for rewriting a HEADING: a heading's per-user expand/collapse state is keyed by its id, and replacing a heading via delete+insert would assign a new id and silently lose that state. It is also the only way to add inline formatting that replace_node_text (plain text) cannot express.
- insert_sibling_node: insert content (markdown, converted automatically) as a new block immediately before or after anchor_node_id (position 'before'/'after'). Works at any depth — anchor on a top-level block to add a block, or on an existing list item to add a sibling list item. To append a bullet, the content must be bullet markdown ('- text'); plain 'text' is a paragraph and is rejected as a list sibling. Use this to add paragraphs, list items, headings, etc.
- insert_child_node: insert content as the first ('start') or last ('end') child INSIDE a block-container node_id that carries an id (a list item, task item, or blockquote — NOT a heading/paragraph/code block, which hold only inline text and reject a block child; and NOT bulletList/orderedList, which carry no id — append a bullet with insert_sibling_node on an existing item instead). Use this when the container has no existing child to anchor a sibling on; otherwise prefer insert_sibling_node.
- delete_node: remove the whole block node_id. To change a block's TYPE (e.g. turn a plain paragraph into a task list), use delete_node together with insert_sibling_node.

confirm_shared.description: Set to true only after the user has confirmed they want to change a document other people can see. Leave unset on the first call.

document_id.description: The UUID of the document to edit. You must have editor access to it.

ops.description: The edit operations to apply, in order, as a single atomic change.

anchor_node_id.description: insert_sibling_node: UUID of the block to insert next to.

content.description: Markdown content. insert_sibling_node / insert_child_node: the new block(s). replace_node_contents: inline-formatted text for the node's new content.

new_text.description: replace_node_text: the replacement text (plain text, no markdown).

node_id.description: UUID of the node to target. Used by replace_node_text, replace_node_contents, delete_node, and insert_child_node (the container to insert inside).

original_text.description: replace_node_text: the exact current text to match and replace within the node.

position.description: insert_sibling_node: 'before' or 'after' the anchor block. insert_child_node: 'start' or 'end' of the container's children.

tools.name: edit_document

tools.description:
Read the user's Daily Note for a date: the dated note TK keeps for each day, built from the user's daily-note template when they use one (sections such as To Do, Recently, and Notes for TK). Some users call it their scratch pad. Use this when the user mentions their daily note, scratch pad, or today's note, asks what they wrote on a given day, or before adding to a day. 

The response has 'found': false when that day has no Daily Note yet — this is a normal answer, not an error, and it does NOT create one. To start a day's note with content, call create_daily_note. To ADD to a day that already has one, call this tool with format "json" to get node ids, then edit_document with the returned id — edit_document addresses nodes by ids that only the JSON carries. A 'found': false answer may name an 'older_note' for that date, an earlier kind of dated note: read it with get_document_content when looking back at past days, but never write a day's new content into it.

date.description: The note's date as YYYY-MM-DD, in the user's LOCAL timezone. Required — the server has no timezone, so it cannot resolve 'today' itself; if you do not know the user's local date, ask.

format.description: Response format. 'plain_text' (default) returns the rendered body. 'json' returns the structured Tiptap content, whose node ids are required to target an edit_document op.

tools.name: get_daily_note

tools.description: Get comments on a specific document. Returns both document-level comment threads and inline comment threads (anchored to a text range). Inline threads carry an 'anchor' object whose anchor_text is the exact document text the thread refers to — use it to tell which passage a comment is about instead of guessing. Returns threaded comments with author info. Use when the user asks about feedback, discussion, or comments on a document.

limit.description: Maximum number of comment threads to return (default: 20).

offset.description: Number of threads to skip for pagination.

tools.name: get_document_comments

tools.description: Retrieve the full content of a specific document by its ID or URL. Returns the document title, body text, tags, and metadata. Use this after finding a document via search to read its contents, or pass a TK URL directly to resolve and fetch the document. The response's comment_counts field reports how many document-level and inline comment threads the document has; use get_document_comments to read them.

document_id.description: The UUID of the document to retrieve. Provide either this or url, not both.

format.description: Response format. 'plain_text' returns just the text content, 'json' returns the full document with structured Tiptap content.

url.description: A TK document URL. Supports all document URL formats including https://tk.xyz/notes/<id>, https://tk.xyz/public/notes/<id>, https://tk.xyz/shared/connections/<id>, https://tk.xyz/libraries/<id>/notes/<id>, and others. Provide either this or document_id, not both.

tools.name: get_document_content

tools.description: Get view statistics for a document the user owns. Returns total views, unique viewers, and breakdown by source. Only works for the user's own documents.
tools.name: get_document_engagement

tools.description: Get the heading structure (table of contents) of a document. Returns the hierarchical outline of headings and subheadings, useful for understanding a long document's organization before reading specific sections.

document_id.description: The UUID of the document whose hierarchy to retrieve.

tools.name: get_document_hierarchy

tools.description: Get which libraries a document belongs to. Only works for the user's own documents.
tools.name: get_document_libraries

tools.description: Get documents that reference/mention a specific document (backlinks). Only shows mentions from documents the user has access to.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 10).

offset.description: Number of results to skip for pagination.

tools.name: get_document_mentions

tools.description: Get reactions (emoji responses) on a specific document. 'reactions' are on the note as a whole, aggregated per emoji with who reacted. 'inline_reactions' are anchored to a passage: each entry carries an 'anchor' whose anchor_text is the exact text reacted to, plus its own per-emoji reactions. To find which notes have reactions, use get_popular_documents with sort_by 'reactions' instead of calling this per note.
tools.name: get_document_reactions

tools.description: Get sharing status of a document the user owns: whether it has a public link, and who it's directly shared with.
tools.name: get_document_shares

tools.description: List, browse, or filter documents in a specific library WITHOUT a relevance query. ALWAYS prefer this over search_library_documents when the user wants to enumerate or filter by metadata (tags, author, date) rather than rank by topic similarity. Examples: 'list everything in library X', 'show me my docs tagged Y', 'show me docs by Z in this library', 'what's in this library', 'oldest in here', 'recently updated docs'. Pinned documents always appear first regardless of sort. The user must be a member of the library. Use search_library_documents only when the user has a topic/concept to rank against.

author_name.description: Filter by author name or username (case-insensitive partial match).

include_content.description: Whether to include the full document content. Default is false. When false, a short preview is returned instead. Content here can lag the live document by a few seconds; use get_document_content when you need the current text.

library_id.description: The UUID of the library to enumerate.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-100). Default is 20.

offset.description: Number of results to skip for pagination. Default is 0.

since.description: Only return documents updated on or after this date. ISO format or natural language.

sort_by.description: Sort field. Pinned docs always appear first regardless of sort.

tags.description: Filter by tags (matches any). Tags are private to each note's owner, so this matches only your own notes in the library; other members' notes never match a tag filter.

tools.name: get_library_documents

tools.description: Get the user's own documents ranked by popularity. Sort by views, comments, or reactions. Use when the user asks about their most popular, most discussed, or most viewed content, or which of their notes have reactions or comments at all: only notes with a non-zero count are returned, so this is the one-call way to list every reacted or commented note. Results are capped at limit; while has_more is true, call again with offset advanced by limit.

date_from.description: Start date for filtering (natural language like 'last week' or ISO format).

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 10, max: 100).

offset.description: Number of results to skip, for paging past the limit.

scope.description: Only with sort_by 'reactions': count only reactions anchored to a passage ('inline'), only reactions on the note as a whole ('document'), or both (default). Rejected with any other sort_by.

tools.name: get_popular_documents

tools.description: Get documents from libraries ranked by popularity (comments or reactions). Use when the user asks about trending or popular content in their network. Optionally filter by source (specific library, or all).

date_from.description: Start date for filtering (natural language like 'last week' or ISO format).

library_id.description: UUID of the library to filter by (required when source is 'library').

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 10).

source.description: Filter by source: 'all' for everything, 'library' for a specific library (requires library_id).

tools.name: get_popular_shared_documents

tools.description: Get the most recently updated documents from the user's personal knowledge base. Returns document metadata and a short preview by default (not full content). Use get_document_content to read the full text of a specific document.

include_content.description: Whether to include the full document content in the response. Default is false. When false, a short preview is included instead. Content here can lag the live document by a few seconds; use get_document_content when you need the current text.

limit.description: Maximum number of documents to return (1-100). Default is 20.

offset.description: Number of documents to skip for pagination. Default is 0.

since.description: Only return documents updated on or after this date. ISO format (e.g., '2025-01-15') or natural language (e.g., 'last week', 'yesterday').

tools.name: get_recent_documents

tools.description: List the documents the user has recently opened, most recently viewed first: their own documents and other people's documents they can still open (through a library, a direct share, a profile share, or a public link). Use this to find something the user remembers reading but did not write. Each document includes last_viewed_at and view_count (times opened in the date window). Returns document metadata and a short preview (not full content). Use get_document_content to read the full text of a specific document.

limit.description: Maximum number of documents to return (1-100). Default is 20.

offset.description: Number of documents to skip for pagination. Default is 0.

since.description: Only count views on or after this date. ISO format (e.g., '2025-01-15') or natural language (e.g., 'last week', 'yesterday').

tools.name: get_recently_viewed_documents

tools.description: Get libraries the user is a member of, with their role and member/document counts.
tools.name: get_user_libraries

tools.description: Remove a document from one library. The document itself is not deleted, and it stays in any other libraries it belongs to; it just stops being visible to that library's members. Allowed when the user owns the document, or is an owner or moderator of the library. Confirm with the user before removing a document they don't own.

document_id.description: The UUID of the document to remove.

library_id.description: The UUID of the library to remove the document from.

tools.name: remove_document_from_library

tools.description: Search within a specific document for matching text passages. Use this to find specific information inside a long document without reading the entire content.

document_id.description: The UUID of the document to search within.

limit.description: Maximum number of matching passages to return (1-50). Default is 10.

query.description: The text to search for within the document.

tools.name: search_document_content

tools.description: Search through the user's personal knowledge base documents. Supports full-text search, semantic (meaning-based) search, and hybrid search that combines both approaches. Use this to find documents by topic, keyword, or concept.

date_range.description: Filter by date range. Use natural language like 'last week', 'past 3 months', 'since January 2025', or ISO dates like '2025-01-01..2025-06-30'.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-100). Default is 20.

query.description: The search query. For fulltext mode, keywords work best. For semantic mode, natural language questions or descriptions of concepts work well.

search_type.description: The type of search to perform. 'fulltext' matches exact words, 'semantic' matches meaning, 'hybrid' combines both (default).

tags.description: Filter results to documents with any of these tags.

tools.name: search_documents

tools.description: Search for libraries by name or description. Returns libraries the user is a member of and discoverable libraries that match the query. Use this to find a specific library or discover new ones.

query.description: Search query to match against library names and descriptions.

tools.name: search_libraries

tools.description: Search documents in a specific library by relevance to a query string. ONLY use this when the user has a topic, question, or concept to rank against. For listing or filtering by tags/author/date WITHOUT a relevance query (e.g. 'show me my docs tagged X', 'list everything', 'oldest first'), use get_library_documents instead. The user must be a member of the library. Supports full-text, semantic, and hybrid search.

author_name.description: Filter by author name or username (case-insensitive partial match).

library_id.description: The UUID of the library to search within.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-100). Default is 20.

tags.description: Filter results to documents with any of these tags. Tags are private to each note's owner, so this matches only your own notes in the library; other members' notes never match a tag filter.

tools.name: search_library_documents

tools.description: Search through documents shared with the user — from libraries or direct shares. Use the 'source' parameter to control which sharing mechanisms to search (default: 'all'). When source is 'all' or 'libraries', results may include the user's own documents that are in libraries. Results include author information. Use this when the user asks about content from teammates, friends, or shared collections.

author_name.description: Filter results to documents by a specific author (case-insensitive partial match on name or username).

date_range.description: Filter by date range. Use natural language like 'last week', 'past 3 months', 'since January 2025', or ISO dates like '2025-01-01..2025-06-30'.

library_ids.description: Filter results to documents in these specific libraries (UUIDs). Use get_user_libraries to discover library IDs.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-100). Default is 20.

query.description: The search query. Keywords, natural language questions, or descriptions of concepts all work.

search_type.description: The type of search to perform. 'fulltext' matches exact words, 'semantic' matches meaning, 'hybrid' combines both (default).

source.description: Which sharing mechanism to search. 'all' (default) searches libraries + direct shares. 'libraries' for all your libraries. 'direct' for documents shared directly with you.

tools.name: search_shared_documents

tools.description: Update an existing document in the user's personal knowledge base. Only the document owner can update a document. Provide only the fields you want to change; omitted fields are left as-is. Provide 'content' (markdown, converted automatically) as the full new body — it REPLACES the entire body (revision history is preserved). This is a whole-document replace, not a merge: any text in the current document that is not in your new content will be removed. If the document is open in the user's editor, the replacement is applied live without a reload, so it will also drop unsaved edits the user is mid-typing. Before updating a document the user may be actively editing, fetch the current body with get_document_content and include anything worth keeping in your new content. To change only PART of a document (a section, a paragraph, a sentence) rather than rewriting the whole body, use edit_document instead — it merges safely with concurrent edits. 'title', when given, becomes the document's first heading. The new body MUST be passed in the 'content' parameter as markdown; calls with unrecognized parameters are rejected. The response includes content_length and heading/paragraph counts of the resulting document — verify these match what you sent. SHARED DOCUMENTS: if anyone else can already see the document — a direct share, a public link, profile sharing, or a library with other members — the first call changes nothing and returns an error saying how it is shared. Tell the user, and ask whether to go ahead; only after they agree, call again with confirm_shared: true. Never set confirm_shared without asking the user first. Updates take effect immediately, including in an open editor.

confirm_shared.description: Set to true only after the user has confirmed they want to change a document other people can see. Leave unset on the first call.

content.description: New body for the document in markdown format (without the title). Replaces the entire document body while preserving revision history.

document_id.description: The UUID of the document to update. Must be owned by the authenticated user.

tags.description: New set of tags for the document. Replaces all existing tags.

title.description: New title for the document. Becomes the document's first heading.

tools.name: update_document
